title: Canonical coefficient and polynomial inclusions between Tate algebras
statement: Let $K$ be a nonarchimedean normed field [def-weil-field] and let $r,s\ge0$. Put $T=K\langle X_1,\ldots,X_r\rangle$ and $D=K\langle X_1,\ldots,X_r,Y_1,\ldots,Y_s\rangle$, using the restricted-series subrings [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation]. Renaming each $X_i$ as the same first coordinate in $D$ preserves restrictedness: the coefficient indexed by an old exponent vector is unchanged and every exponent involving a $Y$ has coefficient zero. The canonical coefficient homomorphism $\iota:T\to D$ is this formal-series renaming restricted to $T$, and the $T$-algebra structure on $D$ is induced by $\iota$. Put $P=T[Y_1,\ldots,Y_s]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. The canonical $T$-algebra homomorphism $\eta:P\to D$ evaluates coefficients by $\iota$ and each polynomial variable at the corresponding last variable of $D$. For any ideal $J\subseteq P$, the canonical quotient $T$-algebra homomorphism $\bar\eta:P/J\to D/(J D)$ sends $[p]$ to $[\eta(p)]$, where $JD$ is the ideal generated by $\eta(J)$, and quotient algebras are as in [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Zero values of $r$ and $s$ are allowed.
